output.myth: When Ennu had no more nets to mend, he carved a gull from the jawbone of a whale that Orrun had cast onto the north shore. He gave it a short neck and a round body, and he cut its wings from goat-hide, stretched and smoked until it stopped smelling of goat. Then he sang to it, which is the only way to make a thing fly. The gull lifted off the rock the first time he let go. Hesk, who winds every string at the pole and keeps the count of those gone aloft, heard it pass over and asked it for the names. The gull could not speak, so it flew, and the wind carried each name up the line into Hesk's reel. Tavo tried to tear its wings once, laughing, and failed. Your grandfather's name is in there somewhere, if the wind was kind. Go and ask Hesk, but keep your hands off the line.
